original_question: Let N_α(d) denote the maximum number of equiangular lines in R^d with common angle α. Is it true that N_{1/5}(d) = 276 for 23 <= d <= 185, and N_{1/5}(d) = floor(3(d - 1)/2) for d >= 185?
target_in_paper: Section 3.8, Conjecture 3.30 (the Lemmens-Seidel conjecture for equiangular lines with parameter 1/5). ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
correct_elements: You identified the exact extremal quantity N_{1/5}(d), the correct dimension ranges 23 ≤ d ≤ 185 and d ≥ 185, and the exact two conjectured values 276 and floor(3(d - 1)/2). Up to a small notation issue about what α means, your draft is essentially a restatement of Conjecture 3.30. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient setting should be stated explicitly: d is an integer at least 1, the lines lie in R^d, and the inner product is the usual Euclidean inner product. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

The paper defines equiangular lines via unit vectors v_1, ..., v_n representing the lines, with ⟨v_i,v_j⟩ = ±α for all i ≠ j; that realization is implicit in your draft but should be made explicit in a stand-alone version. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

In the paper's notation, α is not literally the geometric angle; it is the common absolute inner-product value. Thus α = 1/5 corresponds to common angle arccos(1/5). Your phrase 'common angle α' should be corrected. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

The quantifiers should be explicit: the first equality is asserted for every integer d with 23 ≤ d ≤ 185, and the second for every integer d ≥ 185. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
refined_question: For α ∈ (0,1) and an integer d ≥ 1, let N_α(d) denote the maximum n for which there exist unit vectors v_1, ..., v_n ∈ R^d such that ⟨v_i,v_j⟩ = ±α for all distinct i,j (equivalently, n equiangular lines in R^d with common angle arccos(α)). Is it true that N_{1/5}(d) = 276 for every integer d with 23 ≤ d ≤ 185, and that N_{1/5}(d) = floor(3(d - 1)/2) for every integer d ≥ 185?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper's actual target. Section 3.8 first defines equiangular lines, the quantity N_α(d), and the role of the parameter α via unit vectors in R^d, and then immediately states Conjecture 3.30 with exactly the two formulas in your draft. The only substantive cleanup needed is to make the definition fully self-contained and to correct the phrase 'common angle α' to the paper's convention where α = |⟨v_i,v_j⟩|, so the geometric angle is arccos(α). Just after the conjecture, the paper notes that these results can be reformulated in terms of Seidel matrices with smallest eigenvalue -5, but it does not present a separate numbered equivalent conjecture there, so the equiangular-lines formulation is the closest paper-faithful stand-alone version. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
